rows.comment: Cute phrasing hides the fact: the session has one minute of heart rate.
lineComments: Title says the same thing as a flourish; state the count.
rows.replacement: 'Only one minute of heart rate'

rows.comment: 'Gaps are expected' answers a worry nobody raised, and 'the part it could see' is filler.
lineComments: 'Found a pulse' is vague; say the band recorded heart rate, with the counts.
'Gaps are expected' reassures against an unraised concern.
Restates that the chart shows the recorded part; say it once, directly.
rows.replacement:
'The band recorded heart rate in $have of $total minutes. '
'The chart shows those minutes.'

rows.comment: 'A point, not a line' is an aphorism; state the requirement.
lineComments: Replace the antithesis with what a chart needs.
rows.replacement: 'A line needs at least two minutes of heart rate.'

rows.comment: 'Pulse reading' is a synonym for heart rate used elsewhere; use one term.
rows.replacement: 'No heart rate recorded for this ${a.name.toLowerCase()}'

rows.comment: 'Reported nothing' is vague about what is missing.
rows.replacement: 'The band sent no heart rate during this session.'

rows.comment: Em dash and 'handed over' are flourish.
lineComments: Split at the dash and say 'recorded'.
rows.replacement: 'Partial trace. The band recorded $pct% of these minutes.'

rows.comment: States a number and threshold plainly.
'1RM' is undefined jargon; spell out one-rep max.
lineComments: Weight value and unit stay unchanged.
rows.replacement:
'Estimated one-rep max '
'${_u!.weightValue(rm!).round()} lb'
'Estimated one-rep max ${rm!.round()} kg'

rows.comment: Say what is counted and what is not in one clause.
rows.replacement: 'Sets without a load add to the set and rep totals and add nothing to volume.'

rows.comment: Repeats the title with a count of zero.
'A point, not a line' is an aphorism.
rows.replacement: 'A line needs at least two minutes of heart rate.'
'This session has no per-minute data.'

rows.comment: File path for the tile cache.

lineComments: Say what to enter and in what order.
rows.replacement:
'Enter five thresholds in bpm, lowest first. Each one is where '
'a zone starts. Clear all five to return to the '
'computed zones.'

rows.comment: Error says what to do; tighten.
rows.replacement:
'Enter all five thresholds, lowest first. '
'Nothing was saved.'

rows.comment: Error states the rule and the outcome; thresholds unchanged.
lineComments: States the rule and 30 bpm floor.

rows.comment: 'Come off your age' is loose; say the zones use age. Keep the leading space.
lineComments: Name the actor and the input.
rows.replacement: ' Until the band measures one, the zones below use your age.'

rows.comment: 'A one-second spike is not a heart rate' rebuts a claim nobody made. The 15 second rule is kept.
lineComments: Keep the 15 second and movement condition.
Drop the rebuttal and keep the rule in one sentence.
Remaining fragment of the cut sentence.
rows.replacement:
'A reading counts toward your maximum only if the band held it '
'for 15 seconds while you were moving.'

rows.comment: 'Not a limit', 'creeps up' and the em dash are flourish. Keep the safety note against testing it.
lineComments: Define the value and when it rises.
Keep the instruction not to test it.
rows.replacement:
'The highest heart rate the band has recorded for you. It rises '
'when the band records a harder effort. Do not push to raise it.'

rows.comment: 'Nothing to take a percentage of' is a cute turn; say what is needed.
lineComments: Say the age is the missing input.
rows.replacement:
'Zone edges are percentages of a maximum heart rate. '
'The app estimates that maximum from your age.'

rows.comment: Convoluted sentence; likely a screen-reader label. State the cause.
lineComments: Say zone edges need an age.
rows.replacement: 'Zone edges need your age.'

rows.comment: Button label that says where to go.
Drops 'these are the usual bands, not your own measured thresholds', which rebuts an unraised claim. Keeps numbers and interpolations.
lineComments: Interpolations for resting rate and nights stay.
Keep the zone 1 effect; drop the rebuttal.
rows.replacement:
'Built from your resting rate (${d.restingHr}, the middle of your last ${d.restingDays} '
'nights) and the highest heart rate the band has recorded for you ($max). '
'A low resting rate '
'makes zone 1 wide.'

rows.comment: 'Fits you better' is vague and the closing rebuttal answers nothing. State the mechanism.
lineComments: Keep the night threshold and count.
Say what happens at that point.
rows.replacement:
'Built from the highest heart rate the band has recorded for you ($max). After '
'${d.restingMinDays} nights of resting rate (you have '
'${d.restingDays}), '
'your resting rate is also used. '
'Zone 1 then adjusts to it.'

rows.comment: The repo documents the estimate as Tanaka, 208 - 0.7 x age (zones.dart header, zones l10n key activityZonesAnchorTanaka). No file backs the 20 bpm error figure, so it stays as the existing stated number and is not strengthened.
lineComments: Name the formula used in the repo for the estimate.

rows.replacement:

'They replace the age-based and measured zones.'

Dangling tail of the cut sentence.
rows.replacement:
'The bars appear once the zone edges above are measured. '
'Until then they would only reflect the age estimate.'
